newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast light crude prices trim gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast light crude prices trim gains.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast light crudes trimmed early gains and ended lower along with West Texas Intermediate (WTI), while rumours continued of a Alaska crude deal.
November cash WTI fell 20 to 25 cents from Wednesday, as buyers sought other grades ahead of Friday's pipeline scheduling deadline.

Outright prices for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude tracked WTI and dropped 20 to 25 cents, leaving the grade at $22.05/22.45 a barrel in late trade. But official discounts for ANS remained unchanged at $2.30 a barrel under November WTI.
A cargo of Koch Alberta crude was rumoured to be offered into the West Coast, traders said. The grade competes with ANS.
Traders said buying could increase for San Joaquin heavy crudes, as players scrambled to fill increased space on California's Line 63.
ARCO said Wednesday it would limit the line's crude oil shipments to 60.82 percent of amounts requested, up from 46.06 percent permitted last month.
Traders said additional heavy crudes could weaken demand for more expensive basin grades such as Wilmington.
Wilmington crude held at $18.90/19 a barrel on Thursday.
Kern River heavy crude also held, ranging $17.40.17.60 a barrel, with a major and large independent refiner rumoured to offer cargoes.
